items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: I loved Chet, Blue Mitchell, Art Farmer. I like the cats that played the pretty stuff.

ctx.x: How do you make them right?

By knowing, by having the amount of information in your head of what sounds right and what doesn’t sound right in the bebop tradition. Or even the blues. Understand something, up until the — I would say the inception of jazz, if you want to talk about it from 1917, if you want to talk about the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, but baloney. If we want to talk about ragtime music and improvised music coming out of New Orleans, up until even up to the 60s, by-and-large most of the music, the improvisations were…

we’re just playing by ear. They’re playing by ear. I mean they understand the chord changes most definitely. And I think it’s important for us to learn it, but in the event of a person who’s learning it by ear how do I explain how Stan Getz can play on all of those Chick Corea tunes on that recording “Captain Marvel” when he didn’t know how to read chord changes. And you could hear it, you could hear. Sometimes he deals with things in a certain way. Same thing with Chet Baker. I mean all of those recordings of…
